question.value: What are the morphology and kinematics (rotation, in-fall, central mass, accretion rate, orientation) of the L1527 gas envelope from C18O(2-1) emission, using a simple axisymmetric 3D parameterisation avoiding absorption-dominated regions?

evidence.quote: we have reconstructed its morphology and kinematics under the assumption of axisymmetry about the west-east axis.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00647.S.
Using ALMA observations of the C$^{18}$O(2-1) line emission of the gas envelope of protostar L1527
the longest baseline being 783.5 m
The synthetized beam size (FWHM) is 0.6 $\times$ 0.5 arcsec$^2$ with a $-174^\circ$ position angle from north.
The rms value of the peak varies between 3 and 5 mJy beam$^{-1}$
The time spent on source was 36 minutes.
The observations used in the present article were made in cycle 1 of ALMA operation on July 20, 2014.

method.value: Continuum Gaussian fits to define origin; effective noise per velocity bin from the low-value peak of flux density distribution, offset-corrected

evidence.quote: We evaluated the position and width of the effective noise, meaning the peak observed at low values in the distribution of the flux density, in each velocity bin separately.
We normally retain for the analysis, unless specified otherwise, flux densities exceeding twice the uncertainty (we speak of a 2-$\sigma$ cut).

method.value: Symmetrised data fit with effective-emissivity model with gas spiralling on paraboloids, rotation and in-fall; chi2 minimisation; velocity bins 0-0.32 km/s excluded

evidence.quote: we describe the flux as spiralling on paraboloids having as axis the symmetry axis.

key_parameters.value: chi2 uncertainties: quadrature of noise uncertainties and 10% of flux density; line-of-sight integration to 7 arcsec

evidence.quote: The $\chi^2$ is evaluated using as uncertainties the sum in quadrature of the above mentioned uncertainties and 10% of the measured flux density.

assumptions.value: Axisymmetry about x axis, symmetry in x and y, optically thin C18O

evidence.quote: We assume perfect symmetry in both $x$ and $y$ and rotation invariance about the $x$ axis.

fitting.value: chi2 best fit; parameter sensitivity as change for 5% chi2 increase

evidence.quote: amounts by which the parameter has to increase ($\Delta^+$) or to decrease ($\Delta^-$) for $\chi^2$ to increase by 5%

validation.value: Compared model and data maps and asymmetry; different reasonable choices give same results

evidence.quote: We have checked that different reasonable choices essentially lead to the same results as presented below.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive central mass and accretion rate

method.value: Energy conservation V_tot = sqrt(2GM/r) at 1.5 arcsec; accretion rate from normalisation rho_0

evidence.quote: The measured velocity $V_{tot}$=1.3 km s$^{-1}$at $r$=1.5 arcsec being then equal to $\sqrt{2GM/r}$
we assume a constant temperature of 30 K and a C$^{18}$O to molecular hydrogen ratio of 4.9 10$^{-8}$

results_numeric.quantity: Tilt about line of sight from mean velocity map

evidence.quote: corresponding to a tilt of $\tan^{-1}(0.17)=9.6^\circ$ east of north

findings_qualitative.value: Strong depression of in-falling flux near the disc plane giving X-shaped flow, possibly from CO freeze-out

evidence.quote: evidence for a strong disc plane depression of the in-falling flux resulting in an $X$ shaped flow possibly caused by the freeze-out of CO molecules on dust grains

claims.hypothesis: Envelope kinematics can be measured from non-absorbed regions only
claims.experiment: Parametric axisymmetric model fitted to C18O(2-1) cube
claims.result: Mean in-fall 0.43 km/s, no strong r-dependence; rotation toward Keplerian
claims.finding: Model reproduces data better than earlier attempts; no sudden in-fall jump needed

evidence.quote: no evidence for the sudden jump to $\sim$1.5 km s$^{-1}$required by (cite: Ohashi2014)

claims.hypothesis: Central mass and accretion rate consistent with earlier estimates
claims.finding: Mass agrees with Tobin; accretion about half of Tobin's

evidence.quote: a factor of nearly 2 smaller than obtained by (cite: Tobin2012) from luminosity arguments

limitations_admitted.value: Analysis too distant from star to observe the disc; delta values are not rigorous uncertainties

evidence.quote: However, the range explored is too distant from the star to allow direct observation of the disc.

referee_caveats_inferred: Delta parameter errors are not true uncertainties
Absorption exclusion and ad hoc symmetrisation may bias results
Temperature fixed at 30 K and ad hoc effective emissivity
No comparison to radiative transfer modelling
